jobs.title: Senior ICT System Engineer (m/w/d)
jobs.description: Deine Rolle als ICT System Engineer Als erfahrener ICT System Engineer bist du ein essenzieller Teil unseres Teams. Du planst, realisierst und optimierst moderne ICT-Plattformen und stellst deren sicheren, stabilen und leistungsfähigen Betrieb sicher. Mit deinem technischen Know-how, deinem Blick für das Gesamtsystem und deiner lösungsorientierten Arbeitsweise entwickelst du nachhaltige Infrastrukturlösungen für unsere Kunden. Deine Aufgaben Du designst, implementierst und betreibst komplexe System- und Plattformarchitekturen in On-Premises-, Cloud- und hybriden Umgebungen. Du automatisierst Provisionierung, Konfiguration und Betrieb von Infrastruktur mit Infrastructure-as-Code und Configuration-Management-Tools wie Terraform, Ansible oder PowerShell. Du entwickelst Skripte, Tools und Automatisierungen zur Standardisierung von Deployments, Betriebsprozessen und wiederkehrenden Engineering-Aufgaben. Du konzipierst und implementierst CI/CD-Pipelines für Infrastruktur-, Plattform- und Applikationskomponenten. Du betreibst und optimierst virtualisierte und containerisierte Umgebungen, beispielsweise mit VMware, Hyper-V, Docker und Kubernetes. Du integrierst Server-, Netzwerk-, Storage-, Identity- und Security-Komponenten zu stabilen und skalierbaren Gesamtsystemen. Du konzipierst technische Lösungen für Netzwerksegmentierung, DNS, Load Balancing, Reverse Proxies, Firewalls, VPN und sichere Systemkommunikation. Du implementierst Monitoring-, Logging- und Observability-Lösungen und nutzt Metriken, Logs und Traces zur Analyse komplexer Systemzustände. Du analysierst Performance-Probleme, Netzwerkfehler, Ressourcenengpässe und komplexe Incidents bis auf Betriebssystem-, Netzwerk- oder Applikationsebene. Du planst und realisierst Migrationen, Plattform-Upgrades, Systemablösungen und Cloud-Transformationen. Du entwickelst technische Standards und Referenzarchitekturen für wiederverwendbare und automatisierbare Plattformen. Du dokumentierst Architekturen, Konfigurationen, Abhängigkeiten, Betriebsprozesse und technische Entscheidungen nachvollziehbar und praxisnah. Du arbeitest direkt mit Software Engineers, Security Engineers, Architekten und Kundenteams zusammen und übernimmst bei Bedarf die technische Führung innerhalb eines Projekts. Was du mitbringst Mehrjährige praktische Erfahrung als System Engineer, Platform Engineer, DevOps Engineer, Infrastructure Engineer oder in einer vergleichbaren technischen Rolle. Sehr gute Kenntnisse in mindestens einem Server-Betriebssystem-Stack, beispielsweise Linux oder Windows Server. Fundiertes Verständnis von TCP/IP, Routing, DNS, HTTP(S), TLS, Firewalls, Load Balancing und grundlegenden Netzwerkarchitekturen. Erfahrung mit Virtualisierungsplattformen wie VMware vSphere, Hyper-V oder vergleichbaren Technologien. Praktische Erfahrung mit mindestens einer Public-Cloud-Plattform wie Microsoft Azure, AWS oder Google Cloud. Erfahrung mit Infrastructure-as-Code, beispielsweise Terraform, sowie mit Konfigurationsautomatisierung über Ansible, PowerShell, Bash oder vergleichbare Technologien. Gute Scripting- oder Programmierkenntnisse, beispielsweise in PowerShell, Python, Bash oder einer vergleichbaren Sprache. Erfahrung mit Git-basierten Entwicklungs- und Deployment-Workflows. Verständnis moderner CI/CD-Prozesse und Erfahrung mit Plattformen wie GitLab CI/CD, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps oder Jenkins. Erfahrung beim Aufbau, Betrieb und Troubleshooting produktiver ICT-Systeme mit hohen Anforderungen an Verfügbarkeit, Sicherheit und Nachvollziehbarkeit. Fundiertes Verständnis von Identity & Access Management, Rollen- und Berechtigungskonzepten, Secrets Management und grundlegenden Security-Prinzipien. Erfahrung mit Backup-, Restore- und Disaster-Recovery-Konzepten und deren technischer Umsetzung. Die Fähigkeit, komplexe Fehler systematisch einzugrenzen und Probleme über mehrere technische Schichten hinweg zu analysieren. We're looking for a senior IC to own the analog power chain end-to-end across our UXV platforms: from MOSFET commutation simulation through PCB layout to lab validation. You will be the technical reference on power electronics inside our Lausanne engineering hub, unblocking propulsion, airframe, and embedded teams in parallel as we scale from prototype cadence to multi-platform deployment. This is a builder role, not a research seat. You ship hardware. Responsibilities Power Stage Architecture: Lead motor-controller and DC-DC topology across fixed-wing, multicopter, and hybrid UXV platforms. Translate mission constraints into power-chain specification. MOSFET Commutation & Gate-Drive Design: Own the analog switching design: dead-time tuning, gate shaping, switching-loss vs EMI vs thermal trade-offs. Multi-fidelity Simulation: Deploy the full stack: analytical loss budgeting, transient SPICE (LTspice), system-level modelling in PLECS or Simulink. BLDC Drive Stages: Design three-phase inverters with integrated current sensing, protection, Trapezoidal and FOC-aware hardware interfaces. High-Power-Density PCBA: Lead schematic and layout in Altium or KiCad with thermal, parasitics, and EMC engineered in from the first revision. EMI / EMC Engineering: Drive pre-compliance, filter design, and root-cause debug under flight-representative loads. Prototype-to-Production: Take motor-controller PCBAs through revision discipline, DFM, and qualification - closing the loop on field returns. Lab Validation: Execute bench characterization (power analysers, oscilloscopes, thermal imaging, double-pulse testing) and reconcile against simulation. Firmware & Controls Interface: Partner with embedded and propulsion on FOC tuning, current-sense calibration, and the hardware/firmware compensation boundary. Design Authority & Mentorship: Set the bar via design-decision records and reference designs. Mentor 1–2 junior engineers. Candidate Requirements MSc or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, or equivalent. 5+ years of hands-on R&D experience on motor drives, BLDC/PMSM controllers, or high-power-density power electronics. Deep working mastery of MOSFET commutation design : gate-driver selection, dead-time tuning, switching transitions, loss budgets. Proven ownership of at least one motor-controller PCBA shipped from prototype through production (or pre-production qualification) : ideally on drone, robotics, eVTOL, or automotive platforms. Fluency in simulation (LTspice, PLECS, or Simulink) and PCB design (Altium). Strong, hard-earned intuition for EMI / EMC design and debug. Lab-bench discipline: you've personally debugged what simulation missed. Comfort with scale-up iteration speed and end-to-end ownership. English fluent (working language); French is a nice-to-have, not a requirement. Bonus points for: GaN / SiC experience, safety-critical design exposure , applied control theory implemented in hardware, exposure to defense, aerospace, or UAS programmes. jobs.title: Network Developer
jobs.description: Senior Network Developer About Share Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure across Africa (fiber routes, subsea capacity, data centers, cloud on-ramps) into a single intelligence layer. That lets ISPs, hyperscalers and AI companies get connectivity where they need it in seconds, not months. Today, bandwidth is bought and sold through slow, private, one-off deals, with almost no price transparency. We're replacing that with one neutral exchange: an API on top of real infrastructure, with prices set by actual supply and demand. It's already live across East Africa, with thousands of kilometers of fiber, 12 infrastructure providers, 10 data centers, and around 8 million people served. The Role Our network is the foundation of the product. Every route a customer provisions through our API has to exist, perform and stay up on real hardware. We're hiring a Senior Network Developer to design and build that network as software: a distributed, multi-provider fabric that engineers change through code, not by logging into devices. You'll own the network architecture end to end. That covers our BGP edge (transit, peering at KIXP and LINX, private interconnects with hyperscalers), the backbone, and the PoPs and data centers we're adding across the continent. You'll set the standards our network is built to, which partner ISPs connecting to us will inherit. As we grow, you'll also help build the network engineering team. What you'll do Design the backbone and PoP architecture as standard, repeatable building blocks, from edge to data center, so we can add capacity and new markets without redesigning each time. Drive our move to Segment Routing and a clean IP architecture, including IPv4 reuse, IPv6, and how customer and internal address space coexist. Build on disaggregated white-box hardware (Edgecore with IP Infusion OcNOS today), and make the hardware and software calls that keep us fast and affordable. Turn operations into software. That means a source of truth (Nautobot), templated config (Jinja), and CI/CD with validation, staged rollouts and rollback for every change. Build the telemetry and observability that show what the network is really doing. Use AI where it actually helps: anomaly detection, automated triage, and auto-remediation with a human in the loop. Own availability. Limit how much any failure can affect, mitigate first and diagnose second, and turn post-mortems into fixes in the system. Work with our software team on the API and provisioning layer that exposes the network to customers, and with partner ISPs' engineers on the hand-off. Help hire and develop the engineers who'll run this with you. Our Ideal Candidate 8+ years building and operating large networks at a hyperscaler, CDN, internet exchange, carrier or ISP. Deep BGP at scale: route policy, communities, RPKI, traffic engineering, peering and transit. Strong data center and backbone design. You know Clos/EVPN-VXLAN fabrics and MPLS or Segment Routing, and when each makes sense. Hands-on with white-box or disaggregated networking, including choosing hardware and knowing where the silicon limits you. You treat the network as code. You write automation yourself (Python or similar), and you've built or run the pipelines, source of truth and telemetry that make that safe. You've owned availability for something that couldn't go down, and can walk us through a real incident: what broke, how you found it, and what you changed. AI-native in how you work. You've built with these tools, not just used them, and you have a view on where they help in operations and where they don't. You think like an owner. You bring ideas, not tickets, and you want to help build a team, not just a network. A clear, direct communicator who's comfortable with partners' engineers and with our founders. Nice to have Experience at an internet exchange, or running peering at scale. Open networking stacks like SONiC, OcNOS or FRR, or contributions to them

jobs.title: Network Operation Engineer
jobs.description: Network Operations Engineer 1. About the role Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure into a single layer and give ISPs, hyperscalers, and AI companies a clean path to deliver connectivity into every home and business across Kenya and the continent. Behind that marketplace is a real network: a BGP edge peering with Tier 1 transit, hyperscalers, and local exchanges, an MPLS backbone, aggregation and access gear, and the systems that watch all of it. For the partners who run on us, the network is the product, and the NOC is where they feel it. A clean shift is a partner who never knew anything happened. That is the bar. We are early and the team is small, so we cannot afford a pair of hands that only knows how to escalate. We need a capable network engineer who can stand a shift, resolve real faults without waking anyone, and then keep building the network while East Africa sleeps: propagation and peering checks, health passes across the estate, config changes through to merge, tickets off the board, automation that takes the next repetitive job off everyone's plate. The watching is the floor of this role, not the ceiling. The NOC you would be joining is not a legacy one. We are building it as an AI assisted operations environment from the ground up. The forwarding plane runs on open source routing and forwarding software, every device configuration lives in Git, and an LLM layer sits on top of the live network state. When something moves, that layer reads the telemetry, correlates it against the topology and the config history, and puts a probable cause and a candidate fix in front of the engineer on shift. The point is not to replace your judgment. It is to collapse the time between an alert firing and you knowing where to look, so mean time to repair is measured in minutes. You sit inside that system. You use it, you push back on it when it is wrong, and what you catch that it misses is part of how it gets smarter. As we build automation out across the NOC, you are not just a consumer of the tooling. You help write it. 2. What you'll do Watch, and know what you're looking at. Sit on our monitoring stack (Zabbix and Grafana dashboards, flow telemetry, alerting) and actually read it. Learn what normal looks like so abnormal jumps out at you: a BGP session that dropped, a link that went down, latency climbing on a path, a capacity threshold breached, a partner suddenly pushing or pulling nothing. Troubleshoot and resolve. This is where you earn your seat. Confirm the alert is real, gather the facts, and localise the fault: one peer or many, us or upstream, a real outage or a monitoring blip. The assistive layer surfaces a likely diagnosis and a suggested fix, the config history is right there in Git, and the runbooks are live. Your job is to read all of it critically, decide what is actually true, and close out what you can on your own. Every ticket you resolve yourself is one our senior people did not get pulled out of deep work, or out of bed, to deal with. Keep the network healthy, not just alive. A quiet shift is not an idle one. Run the proactive passes: check that routes are propagating the way they should, that RPKI and filter chains are doing their job, that peering and transit sessions are clean across the edge, that no PoP is drifting toward a capacity wall. Catch the slow degradations that never trip an alert. The day team should inherit a network in a known good state. Build and automate. The repetitive parts of this job should not stay repetitive. Write the scripts that turn a manual check into a scheduled one. Push our config automation forward (Jinja driven generation, NAPALM or NETCONF/gNMI against the devices) so changes ship from data, not from memory. When the assistive layer keeps missing the same thing, that is a candidate for automation, and you are well placed to build it during the hours nobody else is online. Move the work forward. You are part of the network team

We're looking for an engineer who wants considerably more responsibility than "implement what's in the ticket". You'll take an ambiguous problem, shape it together with product, make the important technical decisions, ship it, and stay close enough to see whether it worked. We expect you to have opinions. We also expect you to be good enough to change them. The problem we're solving Large organisations are remarkably good at accumulating problems. A company with 100,000 employees can have thousands of operational challenges across its business units. Somewhere outside that organisation, a startup has probably already built part of the solution. Getting those two things to meet still happens through spreadsheets, long email threads, and meetings whose primary output is another meeting. GlassDollar OS is the operating system for venture clienting: problem → startup discovery → evaluation → PoC → adoption, in one repeatable workflow. Our customers are some of Europe's largest organisations, so the software has to move quickly and behave like something an enterprise can depend on. That tension creates the interesting engineering problems. What we're looking for You can take a problem further than the ticket. Work often starts with something incomplete, like "customers need a better way to manage X". You'll shape the problem with product, challenge assumptions, and decide what belongs in this iteration. Strong opinions about what we build, not only how, are expected here. You care about product. You want to know who you're building for, why the problem matters, and what success looks like. That context should shape your technical decisions. You have technical judgement. There is rarely one correct architecture. You know when the boring solution beats the ambitious one, when an abstraction helps and when it hides the problem, and when a small feature is about to create six months of technical debt. We expect you to reason about API boundaries, data models, permissions, performance, failure modes, testing, observability, and rollout, and to raise concerns with a clear argument attached. You make the system better, not just the feature. You fix the spreading pattern rather than the single instance, make an API easier for the next person, and improve tests because the current setup makes everyone afraid to deploy. Your impact should show beyond the pull requests with your name on them. You can work across the stack. A feature might run from a React interaction through GraphQL into a Node service, a schema redesign, a permissions update, and a safe migration for existing customers. Curiosity to follow the problem matters more than equal depth everywhere. You own quality. We have QA. That's not where quality begins. What breaks if this request happens twice? What happens with old data, or when the API fails halfway through? We use Playwright and Jest alongside reviews and monitoring. The goal isn't coverage, it's confidence. You communicate like your decisions will matter later. Six months from now, somebody should understand an important decision without digging through seventeen Slack messages and a deleted Notion comment. That means writing things down when they matter, explaining trade-offs clearly, giving useful code reviews, and surfacing risks before they become incidents. You raise the engineering bar around you. You do not need a management title to have influence. Find the hole in an architecture, unblock someone without taking the keyboard away, disagree without turning every decision into a referendum. As you earn trust, you’ll naturally become the person people bring harder problems to. jobs.title: Research Staff, Voice AI Foundations
jobs.description: Company Overview Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram. Company Operating Rhythm At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance. Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do. Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5. The Opportunity Voice is the most natural modality for human interaction with machines. However, current sequence modeling paradigms based on jointly scaling model and data cannot deliver voice AI capable of universal human interaction. The challenges are rooted in fundamental data problems posed by audio: real-world audio data is scarce and enormously diverse, spanning a vast space of voices, speaking styles, and acoustic conditions. Even if billions of hours of audio were accessible, its inherent high dimensionality creates computational and storage costs that make training and deployment prohibitively expensive at world scale. We believe that entirely new paradigms for audio AI are needed to overcome these challenges and make voice interaction accessible to everyone. The Role As a Member of the Research Staff, you will pioneer the development of Latent Space Models (LSMs), a new approach that aims to solve the fundamental data, scale, and cost challenges associated with building robust, contextualized voice AI. Your research will focus on solving one or more of the following problems: Build next-generation neural audio codecs that achieve extreme, low bit-rate compression and high fidelity reconstruction across a world-scale corpus of general audio. Pioneer steerable generative models that can synthesize the full diversity of human speech from the codec latent representation, from casual conversation to highly emotional expression to complex multi-speaker scenarios with environmental noise and overlapping speech. Develop embedding systems that cleanly factorize the codec latent space into interpretable dimensions of speaker, content, style, environment, and channel effects -- enabling precise control over each aspect and the ability to massively amplify an existing seed dataset through “latent recombination”. Leverage latent recombination to generate synthetic audio data at previously impossible scales, unlocking joint model and data scaling paradigms for audio. Endeavor to train multimodal speech-to-speech systems that can 1) understand any human irrespective of their demographics, state, or environment

The scope of this work varies by engagement. Some programs require standing up a governed data platform to centralize sensor or operational data from known sources, where the problem is well-defined and the priority is building and shipping. Others involve consolidating data across hundreds of interconnected government systems of record with overlapping schemas, deeply interdependent data flows, and significant architectural complexity. You should be comfortable building independently against defined problems and growing into more ambiguous, complex engagements over time. Forward-deployed means aligned with the mission hero, not always on a plane. Most of the work is remote. You'll travel to sites when the engagement calls for it: initial standup, integration work, incident response, training and knowledge transfer. The rest of the time, you'll be on a video call or in a shared chat with that same mission hero. The role is defined by the relationship with the mission hero, not by where you sit. Build and support integrations with existing mission systems. Prior experience integrating with these types of systems is more relevant than experience building on them. Contribute to mapping complex data landscapes. Some engagements involve hundreds of interconnected systems of record with overlapping schemas and deeply interdependent data flows. You'll help trace how data moves across systems and identify dependencies alongside senior engineers and government stakeholders. Build pipelines that move data through classification boundaries, including ingestion, transformation, catalog registration, model/dataset packaging via Zarf, cross-domain transit, and eventual consistency across DDIL conditions. You produce the evidence the mission hero's ISSM/ISSO needs to run this in IL4/IL5. Contribute field feedback back to product and engineering. File issues, write postmortems, and surface what's working and what's breaking in the mission environment. Support training and knowledge transfer. jobs.description: About the Role Elite Editing is seeking experienced freelance journalists and content professionals to support our growing customer reference and case study programs. We call this our Storyteller role, and we are specifically looking for experienced professionals based in EMEA and APAC time zones . Our Storytellers own the storytelling process from interview through finished draft. They lead kickoff calls with our clients and their internal stakeholders, interview their customers and subject matter experts (SMEs), identify the strongest narrative angles within the information they gather, and then write compelling case studies and customer reference stories that adhere to client-specific standards and style guides. This is more than simply working through a list of prepared questions—or turning a transcript into copy. We need skilled storytellers who listen closely, recognize when an answer deserves further exploration, ask intelligent follow-up questions, identify the details that make a story worth telling, and then shape that material into polished, engaging content. Our ideal freelancer has a journalism or professional interviewing background paired with extensive professional writing experience and strong editorial judgment . You should be comfortable speaking with senior business leaders, technical SMEs, and other professionals; able to quickly understand unfamiliar or complex subject matter; and skilled at transforming what you learn into a clear and compelling narrative. Conduct virtual interviews with our clients' customers and SMEs, often involving senior-level or highly technical professionals. Review project background materials and prepare for interviews in advance. Use provided interview guides as a starting point while adapting questions to the conversation. Ask thoughtful, unscripted follow-up questions that uncover meaningful details, examples, outcomes, challenges, and quotable insights. Identify and develop the strongest story angles from interviews, background materials, and client input. Write polished B2B case studies and customer reference stories based on the information you gather, following client-specific briefs, templates, standards, and style guides. Synthesize complex or technical information into accurate, accessible, and engaging narratives for the intended audience. Maintain a professional, confident, and personable presence while representing Elite and our clients on calls. Work collaboratively with Elite's project managers, editors, and other members of the content team throughout the development and revision process. Follow client-specific processes, confidentiality requirements, and project instructions. Job Requirements Successful candidates must: Have substantial professional writing experience , with a portfolio demonstrating the ability to develop clear, engaging, publication-ready content. Have professional experience conducting interviews, preferably in journalism, B2B content, tech, publishing, corporate communications, or a related field . Be located in EMEA or APAC time zones . Have excellent spoken and written English and exceptional verbal communication skills. Be an exceptional listener who can think on their feet and pursue useful lines of questioning in real time. Be comfortable interviewing senior executives, business leaders, customers, and subject matter experts. Be able to absorb unfamiliar information quickly and ask credible, informed questions about complex topics. Have strong editorial judgment and be able to identify the narrative, details, and supporting evidence that will make a compelling story. Be able to synthesize interviews, transcripts, background materials, and client input into a cohesive finished piece. In this role, you’ll reach out to loyal customers who are running low on the products they already know and love, and help them reorder before they run out. These are warm conversations with people who have already bought from us and already like what we sell. You’re not cold calling. You’re the person who calls at exactly the right moment, makes reordering easy, and keeps their routine uninterrupted. This is a base pay + commission position with uncapped earning potential, making it perfect for individuals who thrive in a performance-driven environment. What You’ll Do: Call, text, and email existing customers whose supply is running low, and secure the reorder before they run out. Work an assigned queue of reorder opportunities daily, following the established call and follow-up cadence. Review each customer’s purchase history and order details before you dial, so every conversation is accurate and personalized. Follow up persistently and professionally across phone, SMS, and email to keep customers engaged and drive conversion. Build rapport with repeat customers so they look forward to hearing from you. Maintain accurate records of every customer interaction and sales activity in our CRM. Meet or exceed individual sales targets on a weekly and monthly basis. What You Bring to The Table: Strong work ethic and self-motivation to drive sales results. Comfort and proficiency with manual dialing and reaching out to leads. Excellent communication skills, with the ability to engage customers via phone, email, and text. Comfort working inside a CRM and order management system, with strong attention to detail on customer records. A consultative approach, with the instinct to listen first and sell second. A positive attitude and a passion for sales. Ability to work independently and handle rejection with resilience. Ability to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment. Prior experience in phone sales or telemarketing is a plus, but not required. Technical Must Have’s: We require a stable internet connection (50+mbps Up & down)capable of supporting seamless voice and zoom communications, and data transfer, with an Octane Speed of 20,000 or greater ( https://chromium.github.io/octane/ ). A backup system for power and internet. A fast and reliable laptop or desktop computer, with working camera, and a working noise-cancelling headset. You will be on Zoom with your team throughout the day. Compensation: Base pay 4+% commission on sales revenue (minus refunds). Your commission rate tiers up as you hit higher performance levels, so top producers earn a higher percentage on the same revenue. Uncapped earning potential Weekly and monthly performance bonuses, including top average order value, top weekly sales, QA excellence, and perfect attendance. Schedule: Full time (35-45 hrs per week) Schedules vary between 9:00am and 7:00pm CT Must be available to work weekends Department Outbound Sales Locations Multiple locations Remote status Fully Remote

jobs.description: The objective of this project is to collect a large and diverse dataset of current neutral selfies, head-pose captures, and historical facial images to support machine-learning research and facial recognition model training at TELUS. The collection includes: • Current Neutral Selfies – clean frontal selfies serving as high-quality identity references, with natural variation in appearance and surroundings. • Current Head-Pose Captures – selfies captured in assigned head directions to introduce pose variation. • Historical Images – older photos from participants’ galleries to capture natural aging and long-term appearance changes. The objective of this project is to collect a large and diverse dataset of current neutral selfies, head-pose captures, and historical facial images to support machine-learning research and facial recognition model training at TELUS. To qualify for payment, you must submit a minimum of 20 valid images. The maximum payout is based on 24 accepted images. jobs.title: Assistenz der Geschäftsführung / Executive Assistant (w/m/d)
jobs.description: welche aufgaben warten auf dich? Deine Mission Du behältst auch dann den Überblick, wenn für andere längst das Chaos beginnt? Dann suchen wir dich! Als Assistenz der Geschäftsführung sorgst du dafür, dass sich unsere Geschäftsleitung auf das Wesentliche konzentrieren kann, weil im Hintergrund alles läuft: Organisation, Korrespondenz, Termine, Verträge und die vielen kleinen Alltagsthemen drumherum. Kurzum: Du bist die Person, die unserer Geschäftsleitung den Rücken frei hält. Deine Aufgaben Organisation & Tagesgeschäft Du übernimmst die tägliche organisatorische und administrative Unterstützung unserer Geschäftsführung: Von der Strukturierung des Tagesablaufs bis zu den vielen kleinen Themen, die dazwischen auftauchen und trotzdem nicht liegen bleiben dürfen. Du behältst offene To-dos im Blick: Du hakst proaktiv nach und sorgst dafür, dass Zusagen und Deadlines eingehalten werden, ohne dass dich jemand extra daran erinnern muss. Du bereitest Termine inhaltlich und organisatorisch vor und nach: Du stellst relevante Unterlagen zusammen, hältst Ergebnisse und nächste Schritte fest und sorgst dafür, dass aus einem Gespräch auch tatsächlich Handlung wird. Korrespondenz, kaufmännische & rechtliche Themen Du übernimmst die Bearbeitung und Organisation von Postfächern und Korrespondenz: Du sortierst, priorisierst und beantwortest eigenständig, was du eigenständig beantworten kannst und bereitest den Rest entscheidungsreif auf. Du unterstützt bei buchhalterischen Prozessen: Du unterstützt z.B. beim Prüfen und Zuordnen von Belegen oder der Vorbereitung für die Buchhaltung. Du unterstützt bei rechtlichen und vertraglichen Themen: Du prüfst Verträge, erstellst Vorlagen und recherchierst rechtliche Fragestellungen. Du hältst Fristen nach und sorgst dafür, dass nichts durchs Raster fällt. Kommunikation & Dokumentation Du koordinierst und kommunizierst mit internen und externen Ansprechpartner:innen: Du agierst oft als erste Kontaktperson und behältst dabei die Prioritäten der Geschäftsleitung und des Unternehmens im Blick. Du erstellst Dokumente, Auswertungen und Präsentationen: Du weißt, welche Inhalte überzeugen und direkt verwendet werden können, ohne dass noch groß nachgearbeitet werden muss. was bringst du mit? Du hast Vorerfahrung in der Assistenz der Geschäftsführung bzw. Executive Assistance Du hast einen sicheren Umgang mit allgemeinen kaufmännischen und administrativen Prozessen Du besitzt grundlegende Kenntnisse in buchhalterischen Themen Du hast Erfahrung im Umgang mit Verträgen, rechtlichen Unterlagen und Fristen Du besitzt ein hohes Verantwortungsbewusstsein sowie ein Höchstmaß an organisatorischen Fähigkeiten Du hast eine sehr strukturierte, zuverlässige und eigenständige Arbeitsweise sowie ein hohes Maß an Diskretion Bevor du dich bewirbst: drei kleine Aufgaben, die uns mehr über deine Denkweise verrät als jeder Lebenslauf: Die Geschäftsführung ist unterwegs und nicht erreichbar. Zwei wichtige Termine kollidieren plötzlich, beide Ansprechpartner bestehen auf dem ursprünglichen Termin. Wie triffst du die Entscheidung, wen du verschiebst, und wie kommunizierst du das? Die Geschäftsführung gibt dir kurz vor einem langen Termin eine knappe, unklare Anweisung zu einem wichtigen Thema und ist danach für Stunden nicht erreichbar. Wie gehst du vor, wenn du nicht sicher bist, was genau gemeint war? Du hast einen vollen Tag mit Deadlines geplant, als die Geschäftsführung dir spontan drei neue, unterschiedlich dringende Aufgaben gibt. Wie strukturierst du deinen Tag neu? was bieten wir dir? Du besetzt eine vertrauensvolle Schlüsselrolle direkt an der Seite der Geschäftsleitung mit viel Verantwortung Teilzeit oder Vollzeit möglich – wir finden gemeinsam das passende Modell Das Arbeiten in einem Team mit flachen Hierarchien, kurzen Kommunikationswegen und schnellen Entscheidungen 100% Remote-Arbeit: Arbeite da, wo du dich am wohlsten fühlst mit flexiblen Arbeitszeiten Du hast stets andere Tierliebhaber um dich und freust dich

jobs.description: The Digital Customer Experience Manager supports the execution and continuous optimization of authenticated and unauthenticated digital experiences across web and mobile applications for existing broadband customers.
